intents.summary: Allocate public Terminal versions once per admitted batch, retaining release intent and existing reservations.

Terminal CI Vitest cache: restore a shard's newest saved modules across lockfile edits that leave Terminal's dependencies alone, prune entries a run did not read before saving, and log how the restore matched.
Terminal CI Vitest cache: the prune step now leaves the saved cache untouched, and warns, when it cannot find the directory the unit step wrote.

Kimi models now compact at their real context window instead of the 200k Claude Code assumes for an unknown model: K3.1 Pro gets a 262,144 window (about a 229k compaction threshold) on every plan unless you set a smaller one for the model.
Bundle libatomic with Linux headless CLI runtimes so stock Linux installs can start Node without installing libatomic1, and report sanitized missing-library diagnostics when startup fails.
Hide your offline trust-revoked sign-ins from machine pickers and list_machines, including tunnels left behind, while keeping online, current, and shared computers available.

Leased Personal Claude and Codex keys now stay on this computer when CodePress sign-in changes for the same person: a new token generation, a locally expired token (kept for up to 24 hours) and a 403 that is not about this computer or organization no longer delete them, so workers stop dying with "Not logged in". Turn off `terminal.personalLeaseKeepAcrossAuth` to restore the old behaviour.

Show Terminal tunnel computers in Settings and keep earlier sign-ins revocable under a collapsed Older sign-ins section, preserving the existing list on older backends.
Always keep This computer visible, including when it is revoked.

Leased Personal Claude and Codex keys keep renewing while CodePress's account listing is failing, and a Claude tab or worker launch renews a due leased key first (bounded by the lease request timeout), so a worker no longer starts on an expired token. A renewal that fails or times out launches on the current token and shows the error on the account.

Cleaning up a landed project's session folder no longer makes a worker relaunch or a new worktree on a busy machine fail with "Could not acquire worktree lifecycle lock": the machine-wide check for running processes in the folder now runs before the shared worktree lock is taken, not while it is held.

The kickoff's Runs on now lists your other machines wherever Auto is offered (including Chat), and Auto no longer hangs on "Auto is choosing where to run": it names its pick within seconds, or falls back to This machine after 2.5 s with a reason. Machine lists load faster and are shared between the Connect menu and the kickoff.

A stuck machine-list request no longer freezes Runs on → Your machines, Chat's Runs on and the Connect menu on their last list: the read gives up after 35 s, the list it had stays (marked stale), and the next poll reads again.
Retry transient Linux CLI delivery-ledger reads within the upload budget and name redacted publication refusals.
Show the hosting Mac's weekly subscription usage in a synced project's Orchestrator and Workers model pickers.

A Claude worker that prints "Not logged in · Please run /login" now recovers by itself: Terminal leases the person's active Personal account again and resumes the worker, or fails the worker over to another healthy account. A Personal lease whose renewal just failed or timed out is no longer waited on again by every launch for a minute.
Use one native activation rule for synced Claude and Codex accounts, preserve outside logins, and explain skipped switches on the Accounts card.
